text:
Erin (Sales): Hey team — acme POC hitting 413 when they POST a zipped context bundle to our embeddings endpoint. Zip file is ~9.2MB, we base64 it in the JSON body and it grows to ~12.3MB. Error from client: "413 Request Entity Too Large". Any quick workarounds?

Leo (SalesEng): Can you paste the exact curl + error and any request-id from logs? Also which endpoint are they hitting (embeddings vs completions)?

Erin (Sales): embeddings endpoint: POST /v1/embeddings. Curl they used:

```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"model":"embed-large","input":"<base64-zip-data-here>"}'
```

Client console shows 413, response body sometimes empty. No request-id in client. They said corporate proxy might be in front of them.

ingress-bot: nginx upstream sent 413, client: 10.2.8.9, server: api.redwood.ai, request: "POST /v1/embeddings HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://upstream:8080/", host: "api.redwood.ai"

Maya (Support): If they're base64-encoding the zip into JSON, overhead is ~33%. 9.2MB -> ~12.3MB is expected. Short-term: ask them to gzip the raw payload and send with content-type application/octet-stream (no base64), or better: presign an S3 upload and send us the URL.

Jamal (Eng): 2 quick checks: our public API has nginx/gateway max-body-size 10MB at the edge for safety. We can raise it but entitles policy and SLA implications. Also proxies in front of client or corporate gateways often cut off earlier.

Priya (ML Eng): Also note embeddings endpoints have token limits, but this is a transport size issue — for chunking we should advise splitting their context into smaller chunks (e.g., 2MB gzipped pieces) and run multiple embedding calls. If they need a single vector, we can recommend client-side aggregation (mean pooling) or server-side re-embedding after concatenation with a server-side presigned download.

Leo (SalesEng): For POC speed: propose this flow to the customer:
1) Upload bundle to secure S3 via presigned URL (we provide).
2) Hit /v1/embeddings with {"model":"embed-large","input_url":"s3://..."} so we pull from S3 internally (or they can do multipart and give us chunk URLs).
This avoids base64 overhead and avoids edge body limits.

Maya (Support): If presign isn't allowed by their security team, quick workaround is multipart POST: split zip into N parts client-side, each <8MB, upload sequentially and stitch results on client. We'll add docs.

Jamal (Eng): If we need to change gateway limits for this specific tenant during the trial, we can temporarily increase client-specific max_body_size on the edge, but Ops approval required. Also note: keeping large JSON bodies hurts throughputs and logging costs (we echo a portion in logs).

Erin (Sales): Good notes. Customer asked about pricing impacts if we accept larger uploads — will increased body sizes affect cost?

Maya (Support): Slightly — larger request/response sizes increase bandwidth and can increase tokenization costs if we end up re-processing. But POC sized uploads occasional won't change pricing tiers. For production, recommend S3 + streaming to minimize unit costs.

Priya (ML Eng): Technical checklist for them:
- avoid base64; use binary or presigned S3
- gzip before upload (gzip + binary beats base64-in-json)
- split into ~2–4MB gzipped chunks and embed separately
- include a small manifest if using chunking so we can reassemble or aggregate consistently

Leo (SalesEng): I'll draft a one-pager and quick script (node + curl) for presign + upload flow. Erin — want me to send to acme now?

Erin (Sales): Please do. I'll cc their infra lead and note the temporary options (multipart or gateway bump) if they're blocked on policy. Will try presigned S3 first and report back. :thumbsup:

Jamal (Eng): If they need the gateway bump, tag me and I'll start the change request (we'll need justification and end time).

Maya (Support): Adding a short example they can copy:

```
# upload gzipped binary to our presigned url
curl -X PUT "<presigned-url>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/octet-stream" \
  --data-binary @context.zip.gz
# then call embeddings with pointer
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{"model":"embed-large","input_url":"<s3://bucket/key>"}'
```

Erin (Sales): Perfect — thanks everyone. I'll test presign flow with them this afternoon and update thread.

Leo (SalesEng): lmk if you want me on the call.

Erin (Sales): Will do. End of thread.
